life.replacement.third_bell.S09.en_us.0: Ren stands behind two gate disciples across the only dry exit. The disciples’ blades remain sheathed.
life.replacement.third_bell.S09.en_us.2: Qiao: “Ask why my complaints came back.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S09.en_us.3: Ren: “His complaints asked me to stop the extra draw. I couldn't see how to do that and keep the infirmary open.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S09.en_us.5: Ren: “No. I thought the sleeve would last until the replacement arrived.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S09.en_us.8: Both disciples glance at him. Ren does not repeat himself.
life.replacement.third_bell.S09.en_us.9: Ren: “I’ll record his custody and bring him before Xu. No punishment before the hearing.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S09.en_us.10: Qiao: “You crossed out my wages before this hearing.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S09.en_us.11: Ren: “Then have him ask me about them.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S09.en_us.12: Tao: “There are villagers waiting outside who may be willing to come with us. Their support or an inspection pass would give us grounds to insist Qiao be escorted to the hearing without being arrested.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S09.A: “Record your guarantee. I’ll accompany him into custody.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S09.B: “Ask the villagers to witness this so we can get him to the hearing without a fight.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S09.C: “Stand aside. I’m opening a path for him.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S09.D: “I'll take the report back rather than start a fight here.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S10.title: One Corridor
life.replacement.third_bell.S10.en_us.0: The disciples draw when you step between them and Qiao. Ren backs behind the inspection desk.
life.replacement.third_bell.S10.en_us.1: Ren: “If you fight here, keep away from the sluice. You'll make the repairs harder than they already are.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S10.en_us.4: Tao pulls him behind the stone partition. Neither joins the battle.
life.replacement.third_bell.S10.en_us.5: You: “Let him reach Xu without their hands on him.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S10.en_us.6: Ren: “You can still go with Qiao to the hearing if you let the guards take him into custody.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S10.en_us.7: Both disciples move away from the shaking housing. Ren, a mortal clerk, stays behind the desk.
life.replacement.third_bell.S10.B: “I'll let him go into recorded custody as long as I can accompany him.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S11.title: Empty Buckets
life.replacement.third_bell.S11.en_us.0: Tao opens the outer door. Villagers enter carrying empty buckets instead of weapons.
life.replacement.third_bell.S11.en_us.1: Tao: “We're going with him to the hearing. Keep to the dry stones on the way and leave the controls alone.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S11.en_us.3: Tao: “They've been carrying empty buckets all morning. Did you think they wouldn't come?”
life.replacement.third_bell.S11.en_us.4: A woman puts her bucket down between Ren and Qiao.
life.replacement.third_bell.S11.en_us.5: Woman: “My field can wait a morning. His hearing can’t.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S11.en_us.6: You: “Being here means your names may enter the complaint.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S11.en_us.7: Woman: “Then read mine back before you submit it.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S11.en_us.9: Tao: “Your mother should hear that from you.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S11.en_us.11: Tao: “Walk with us so we can all see where you're taking him. Then we can decide whether to hear this publicly or discuss an agreement in private.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S11.A: “Hear the whole account before the witnesses.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S11.B: “Keep the evidence sealed while we hear the proposals.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S12.title: Whose Price?
life.replacement.third_bell.S12.en_us.0: Du arrives after another healer takes her clinic watch. The discussion happens beside Xu’s regulator, not in a distant council hall.
life.replacement.third_bell.S12.en_us.7: Du: “They were sending nine village patients home. I had no beds.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S12.en_us.10: You: “Did you ask on the eleventh?”
life.replacement.third_bell.S12.en_us.11: Du: “I asked Ren whether they were safe.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S12.en_us.13: Du: “I wanted to believe him when he said they were safe so I let it go without asking again.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S12.en_us.14: Qiao looks down at his bare feet.
life.replacement.third_bell.S12.en_us.15: Ren: “I kept spending the maintenance money. I expected to find another payer.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S12.en_us.16: Xu: “We can put the repairs on the public record and use the reserve to pay for them. The other options are to lease land to fund the work or close the sluice permanently.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S12.en_us.17: Tao: “And people who don’t agree with any.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S12.en_us.18: Xu: “They keep their land. Nobody here has permission to sell it for them.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S12.en_us.19: Du: “Whatever you decide about the money, my son still gets his hearing.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S12.en_us.20: Qiao: “You said a hearing first. Don’t say standing beside my guards was the same.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S12.en_us.21: Qiao: “Xu is here. I’ll sign both sheets now. Not just the one about the nails.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S12.A: “Put the evidence before a public hearing.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S12.B: “Let's ask the owners whether they'd agree to a four-summer lease.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S12.D: “I won’t sponsor any of these agreements.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S13.title: Names on the Record
life.replacement.third_bell.S13.en_us.0: Tao lays the evidence on an upturned flour chest.
life.replacement.third_bell.S13.en_us.1: Tao: “We have the ten-day order and Xu's account of the test along with the counts if we managed to save them. Du, would you confirm that this is your mark on the order?”
life.replacement.third_bell.S13.en_us.2: Du: “I signed the first ten days. I didn’t ask carefully enough about the rest.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S13.en_us.3: Qiao: “I drove the nails. I thought a visible spill would force an inspection.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S13.en_us.4: Xu: “The register would let me certify who authorized the extra draws and issue this restitution order. If we haven't got it I can still close the sluice on the testimony we've heard but the compensation will need stronger evidence.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S13.en_us.6: Xu: “The toll reserve. The infirmary patients must temporarily move into village care.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S13.en_us.7: Du: “I'll ask around for beds. It'll take time; I can't fit everyone in the clinic.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S13.en_us.8: Tao: “And the ruined crop stays ruined. Put that in too.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S13.en_us.9: Tao: “You promised this would stay sealed. Publish it, and I’ll stand by the facts—not by your word.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S13.A: “Publish the full record and accept the resulting inquiries.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S13.B: “Not this ruling. Return to the lease proposal.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S13.C: “We need to consider closing the sluice permanently if it can't keep running safely.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S14.title: The Four-Summer Lease
life.replacement.third_bell.S14.en_us.0: Tao returns with six fieldholders’ signatures. Their reed strips amount to half the village’s reed ground; those who refused retain theirs.
life.replacement.third_bell.S14.en_us.2: Xu: “The sect owes fixed rent as minimum grain to the leasing households. Remaining nursery income supports the infirmary; the toll reserve buys the sleeve.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S14.en_us.4: Xu: “The sect. Minimum grain is written before profit.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S14.en_us.6: Tao: “For once, not just for us.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S14.en_us.8: Xu: “Paid maintenance through those summers, under supervision. Liability for the nails remains in the sealed record.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S14.en_us.10: Xu: “He'll be paid for the work. Ren's salary will stand as security against any further unauthorized draws and Qiao's unpaid wages will remain on the books until they're settled.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S14.en_us.12: Xu: “He'll keep the post under supervision while the inquiry into his spending continues.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S14.en_us.13: Tao: “Two families wanted him dismissed. They won’t thank you.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S14.en_us.14: Qiao: “Will my mother still have patients?”
life.replacement.third_bell.S14.en_us.15: Du: “I hope so. Some of them may not trust me after this.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S14.A: “Witness these terms, without signing for those who refused.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S14.B: “I'd rather discuss permanent closure than agree to this lease.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S14.C: “I'm withdrawing because I can't make guarantees for either side.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S15.title: Two Closed Channels
life.replacement.third_bell.S15.en_us.0: Qiao chalks two lines on the stone: village water, sect water. Across both, he draws a bar.
life.replacement.third_bell.S15.en_us.1: Qiao: “We close both ends before taking the connecting rod out.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S15.en_us.3: Xu: “There won't be another draw and I don't want anyone trying to force the mechanism with a technique.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S15.en_us.4: Tao: “The households have agreed to surrender the shared irrigation right. Some will have to leave their fields.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S15.en_us.6: Xu: “We'll use the reserve to move the patients since we won't be buying a replacement sleeve.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S15.en_us.7: Du: “I’ll go with the village patients until someone receives them.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S15.en_us.9: Tao: “Maybe. But we'd need the money and everyone's agreement all over again. Some families can't afford to wait for that.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S15.en_us.11: Tao: “You can carry messages or call valve positions. Nobody’s asking you to lift brass. Xu, have you given the instruction?”
life.replacement.third_bell.S15.en_us.12: Xu: “Not yet. Are you asking me to proceed?”
life.replacement.third_bell.S15.A: “Proceed with the agreed closure. I’ll do what I safely can.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S15.B: “Wait. I won’t sponsor permanently losing irrigation.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S16.title: The Report Still Owed
life.replacement.third_bell.S16.en_us.0: Back at the clinic, you put the account on the table. Du moves an untouched bowl aside to make a dry place for the papers.
life.replacement.third_bell.S16.en_us.2: Tao: “Enough to know why it happened. Not enough to settle it.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S16.en_us.5: Tao: “With the witnesses. He’s not in custody.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S16.en_us.6: Du: “I want to call you a coward. It would be easier than deciding what I should have done.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S16.en_us.7: Tao: “Xu has ordered a temporary closure. Nobody’s getting the water they expected.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S16.en_us.8: Du: “Tell me what happened, including what went wrong. I need to know what we're dealing with.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S16.en_us.9: Du: “If you want to submit a statement I can give you paper. You're also welcome to stay and help with whatever work your injuries allow.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S16.A: “I’ll stay seven days and do what my body allows.”
life.replacement.third_bell.S16.B: “Send my named statement under seal to the sect’s auditors.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E1.title: A Bell with Witnesses
life.replacement.third_bell.E1.en_us.0: The third bell does not ring. Dead seedlings still streak the fields.
life.replacement.third_bell.E1.en_us.1: Xu: “Once the repairs are done we'll return to two draws a day with a keeper from each side signing every count.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E1.en_us.3: Xu: “Copied outside Ren’s office. His authority to approve draws is suspended pending review.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E1.en_us.4: Du: “I've only found three beds so far and I still need another twenty before we can say everyone's got somewhere to sleep.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E1.en_us.6: Xu: “To go home. Then supervised repairs, and an inquiry into the blocked drain.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E1.en_us.7: Du: “You can keep the room. I know a bed doesn't cover what you've done for us.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E1.en_us.8: Back at the clinic, Qiao first finds his boots beside the stove.
life.replacement.third_bell.E1.en_us.9: Qiao: “Next time someone says wait ten days, I’m writing down who answers on the eleventh.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E1.en_us.10: You retain a witnessed account, not a technique or stones. The village wins enforceable limits, not the season it lost.
life.replacement.third_bell.E1.en_us.11: Tao: “I’ll vouch for the facts. Not for your promises.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E2.title: Four Summers
life.replacement.third_bell.E2.en_us.0: Reed boats pass the new sect nursery.
life.replacement.third_bell.E2.en_us.1: Tao: “They wanted to move the boundary yesterday. I showed them the signed map. They moved the stakes back.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E2.en_us.3: Tao: “I signed because we needed the repairs even though I wish we'd found a way to pay without leasing the land.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E2.en_us.4: Qiao: “They've hired me for maintenance under a supervisor. Now that the sleeve's been replaced the two of us sign off on every count together.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E2.en_us.5: Du: “All twenty-three patients kept their beds. Three families here won’t bring me their sick anymore.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E2.en_us.7: Du: “Where he can be watched. And his salary is still security, not forgiveness.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E2.en_us.8: Tao: “The first grain payment has arrived in advance. The four-summer lease starts now.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E2.en_us.9: Du: “Your room is paid for. Don’t expect a feast.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E2.en_us.10: The agreement has limits and an end date. It has also changed who works the fields, who trusts the clinic, and what Qiao owes his neighbors.
life.replacement.third_bell.E3.title: The Severed Channel
life.replacement.third_bell.E3.en_us.0: When the connecting rod comes free, the bell gives one thin, accidental note.
life.replacement.third_bell.E3.en_us.2: Tao: “That's all we can do under the old agreement. Put the irrigation surrender in the dry box where it won't get wet.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E3.en_us.3: Du: “The other infirmary has confirmed beds for all twenty-three patients. Sect workers will escort them and I'll stay with the nine from our village.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E3.en_us.5: Tao: “Still ours. Nobody gets an empty channel as spoils.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E3.en_us.6: One household loads farming tools onto a cart. Another stays to repair a rain cistern.
life.replacement.third_bell.E3.en_us.8: Tao: “I don't know. Some of them have already started packing.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E3.en_us.9: Qiao: “Boots first. Then I’ll help with the cart and the cistern.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E3.en_us.10: Both channels are disconnected. The feud loses the machinery that sustained it; the village loses its irrigation. No one is paid a repair reward for retiring the structure. Du confirms your report reached her.
life.replacement.third_bell.E4.title: Something Smaller Than Justice
life.replacement.third_bell.E4.en_us.0: Tao leaves his written account at the clinic.
life.replacement.third_bell.E4.en_us.1: Tao: “The temporary closure is still in place.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E4.en_us.2: Du: “We're having to ration water at the clinic while the sect arranges to move its patients. They still haven't agreed to pay for the damage to our fields.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E4.en_us.3: Tao: “The report records whether Qiao was taken into custody or remained free with the witnesses. I haven't changed anything to make our part in it look better.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E4.en_us.6: Du: “I can forgive being afraid. I won’t call it keeping every promise.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E4.en_us.8: Du: “I hope so. Leave a copy here; I don't want it getting lost in someone's office.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E4.en_us.9: She folds the account into a dry box. It cannot clean the well, but anyone investigating will know that Qiao cannot bear all the blame. No additional reward has been set aside for you.
life.replacement.third_bell.E4.en_us.10: Du: “You kept the stove tended. That helped. Don’t pretend it repaired the channel.”
life.replacement.third_bell.E4.en_us.11: Tao: “They received the named complaint. Received isn’t the same as resolved.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.title: Winter Coats for the Dead
life.replacement.winter_coats.S01.title: The Name on the Receipt
The kiln collapse at Stone-Lamp village killed the tailor Duan He's husband Jian Cheng nineteen days ago. She invites you inside and unfolds a winter-coat receipt returned by the accounts office. It reads: Collected personally—Jian Cheng. The collection is dated yesterday.
Duan: “My husband's been dead for nineteen days and someone signed this in his name yesterday.”
You: “Could another man share his name?”
Duan: “Then he shares my address and my husband’s missing thumb.”
She turns the receipt over. A clerk has written: Unable to make a thumbprint.
You: “You think someone stole his allowance.”
Duan: “I don't know yet. But everyone I ask tells me to leave it alone.”
Duan: “I'll pay you two spirit stones to find out what happened. Whatever you learn I'd rather hear it from you than have people whispering about it outside my shop.”
She sets the two stones apart from her rent money.
Duan: “Tell me before you tell the square. I washed his body. I won’t have strangers deciding what happened to him again.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S01.A: “I’ll follow the coats. You’ll hear before the square.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S01.B: “I'll ask the sect and report honestly although I can't promise to keep this private.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S02.title: Beneath the Coffin
Following the delivery note on the receipt, you find the funeral cart outside the village. Its driver Tang Qi is arranging a woolen cloth beneath the coffin, with six food bowls wrapped inside.
Tang: “I know there are six bowls without you counting them out for everyone to hear.”
Tang: “Ask Gu at the old drying house. Quietly.”
Tang: “People also worked there. It has more than one room.”
You: “Why send bowls under a coffin?”
Tang: “Those six are dead on the register. They don't even have names to collect meals under. I use the funeral cart to get food to them.”
He straightens the cloth over them, then stops hiding it.
Tang: “My sister can shelter six adults across the river. I booked tomorrow’s ferry. Tools go free only if they’re loaded before dusk today.”
Tang: “I booked the ferry, didn't I? But every time I start packing, someone else needs the cart.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S02.A: “Take me to Gu. I’ll hear him first.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S02.B: “First, let the sect explain seven death records.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S03.title: Withheld Wages
Pei Xun reads the receipt without touching Jian’s signature.
Pei: “Gu wrote this. He taught me that little hook.”
You: “There are seven workers listed as dead and someone's still collecting in their names.”
Pei: “There's a hundred and forty stones held here: twenty in wages for each of the six workers and another twenty for Jian's death allowance.”
You: “Why hold wages belonging to dead people?”
Pei: “Because there are no bodies recorded for six of them.”
He draws an inspection warrant toward him but leaves it unsigned.
Pei: “Jian’s shift order is in the damaged records bay. The drying house itself is safe. Tang knows which wall not to lean on.”
Pei: “People are waiting at the hall about their wages. I have to see them before it closes, then I'll come. And I can only release money I'm authorized to release.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S03.A: “Issue the warrant. I’ll look for the original order.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S03.B: “I'd like to hear Gu explain his part before I sign anything.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S04.title: One Name, Six Coats
Gu carries broth through a side door, then shuts it with his heel.
Gu: “Is that the receipt they sent back to the tailor yesterday?”
You: “You signed for a dead man.”
Gu: “I collected all six coats under the same name.”
Gu: “I haven't touched his allowance. I claimed surplus coats in his name because the six living workers would have been sent back for reassignment if I'd used theirs.”
A cough comes through the wall.
Gu: “They did. Steward Mu answered that anyone able to stand could sort ore.”
Gu: “I reported seven bodies. Tang buried one.”
Gu: “They asked not to go back. I chose the paperwork.”
He puts his clothing ledger down.
Gu: “Make a copy and have someone witness it. After that report I filed, I wouldn't expect you to trust me.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S04.A: “Tang, copy it. Then we find the shift order.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S04.B: “We can finish the paperwork after the injured people have been seen to.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S05.title: Before the Sixth Cart
Tang guides you around the damaged records room and warns you away from a split beam. A fallen tile pins down Jian's shift order. The circled instruction remains clear: Do not open the vent before the sixth cart is full. Steward Mu's seal is below it.
Tang: “He copied orders twice. Said bosses remembered better with witnesses.”
Tang: “We can use the timber from my cart to take it apart from outside but it'll cost us half a day.”
You: “We’ll miss the ferry cargo deadline.”
Tang: “Then we'll have to decide how to get their tools onto the ferry too. Whatever we work out I'm not sending anyone under that beam to see whether it holds.”
Dust falls through the split. Tang steps back and leaves room for you outside.
Tang: “Without the sealed original, they’ll say the foreman misunderstood.”
Tang: “He can't tell us now. That's why I want the order out of there.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S05.A: “Dismantle it safely. I’ll do what my condition allows.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S05.B: “Retrieve the page from outside with a technique I already know.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S05.C: “Let's leave the records for now and go to the drying house.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S06.title: The Living
Shao Ning sits where the drying racks once stood. Five other survivors mend sacks around him. His sword hand is splinted.
Shao: “If you’re here to see a ghost, be disappointed.”
Shao: “They assigned me to sorting even though I'd shown them I couldn't close my hand.”
Shao: “Still have the root. Still know my technique. Neither fixes this.”
Shao: “Held the door until we got through.”
Shao: “I know. I carried him to Tang.”
You: “Why use his name for your coats?”
Shao: “It was already on the relief list. We told ourselves nobody would lose anything.”
Shao: “She knows Jian was buried, and now she has to ask people about a receipt like that. We should have explained it to her ourselves.”
Shao: “A name I can earn money under. A room without orders attached.”
Shao: “I'll testify in public if we have the sealed order to back it up. Without it I'm only willing to speak privately to Pei and the other five will have to decide for themselves.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S06.A: “Let everyone give a voluntary statement. Then we see Duan.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S06.B: “I'll ask Pei to come here so you can be heard before anyone takes you into custody.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S06.C: “I can’t guarantee their actions. I can bring Pei to listen.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S07.title: Tell Her First
Shao asks to accompany you to the tailor's shop and explain himself. Duan listens to both of you standing up before fetching six pieces of clean lining.
Duan: “Tang bought such cheap wool that everyone wearing one of these borrowed coats has been scratching.”
Duan: “I’m angry. That doesn’t make the wool softer.”
Shao: “I thought you’d ask why he died and I didn’t.”
Duan: “I was going to ask whether he knew the roof would fall.”
Shao: “No. He thought someone would finally open the exhaust.”
She puts the lining beside him, not in his injured hand.
Duan: “He told me he was frightened the roof would fall. I need you to remember he wanted to come home as much as any of you.”
Duan: “I know. That’s why I haven’t thrown you out.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S07.A: “I've brought the report as promised and I'd like you to hear what Pei has to say once we've settled my fee.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S07.B: “Use my two stones to buy them a meal.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S08.title: The Teacher’s Signature
Everyone meets at the old drying house. Pei arrives alone and pauses at the sight of the splint before looking up at Shao's face.
Shao: “You examined that hand before assigning me another shift.”
Pei: “I checked whether you could hold a brush.”
You: “Can you cancel their work orders?”
Pei: “Provisionally. I can’t award lifetime damages.”
Pei: “Once there's a ruling or a settlement I can release the hundred and forty stones we're holding for them. It's their money and they shouldn't have had to wait for it.”
Pei: “A public case with proof closes the working gallery pending inspection. Thirty households lose wages meanwhile.”

Pei: “Under a private settlement they'd receive six months of lodging and paid work suited to their injuries along with the money already held for them. They would have to give up any further accident claims.”
Tang: “Or they come across the river. My sister has two rooms. No promised jobs.”
Pei: “I can authorize departure for these willing claimants before formal custody. Not erase Gu’s false report.”
Shao: “Let us talk it over before you sign anything. All six of us.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S08.A: “Arrange a public hearing. Let each witness decide whether to appear.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S08.D: “I won’t sponsor a solution. Seek supervised lodging and an identity inquiry.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S09.title: The Next Room
Pei goes to register the public hearing, but two early Qi Refining officers arrive first. Their detention order lists the six survivors in connection with the false death reports.
Escort: “We were told they were impostors.”
Shao: “I wish you'd mistaken me for someone with a hand that still worked.”
Escort: “Then show inspection authority and their signed statements. We can substitute a voluntary escort. Otherwise they’re held until he confirms.”
Shao: “We've already told Pei. How many times do we have to do this?”
Tang moves the other five behind the drying-house partition.
Tang: “Choose before somebody reaches for a hilt. They’re not standing here to be used as shields.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S09.A: “Record the custody. I’ll accompany them to the hearing.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S09.B: “Here are the warrant and six statements. Make it a voluntary escort.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S09.C: “You will not take them through this doorway that way.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S09.D: “Bring Pei to negotiate. Accept recorded custody until he arrives.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S10.title: No Other Funeral
The escorts draw their swords when you block the doorway while Tang keeps Shao and his splinted hand safely behind him.
You: “You don’t get them this way.”
Tang: “If you fight, do it in the yard. Don't wreck the room where the injured are staying.”
The escorts follow you onto bare flagstones. Their orders are to restrain, not execute. That does not make a defeat painless.
Shao, from the doorway: “Just get them away from the door. Please don't get anyone killed.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S10.B: “Stand down. I’ll accompany them under recorded custody.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S11.title: Who Pays for Winter?
The hearing takes place outside Duan’s shop, where people already gather for measurements and debt reminders.
Gu: “Steward Mu’s order. Exhaust closed until the sixth cart.”
Shao: “We'd only reached the third cart and Jian had already asked twice for the exhaust to be opened.”
Pei: “My reassignment order followed the collapse. I signed it.”
Duan: “Are you saying that because someone found the page?”
Pei: “You can put my name in the statement. I signed the order; I won't deny it.”
A quarry worker holds up his empty lunch cloth.
Worker: “Close the gallery and what do my children eat?”
You: “No one gets to call the danger imaginary either.”
Pei: “The evidence supports suspension and release of the held money. Further compensation needs another hearing. I won’t write an award I cannot pay.”
Shao: “I said I wanted the order first.”
He does not step before the crowd.
Gu: “I wrote the false report. I can admit that.”
Pei: “We can investigate that report. We cannot enter missing evidence as evidence found.”
Duan: “You said I would hear first. You brought the evidence, but couldn’t spare a sentence for me.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S11.A: “Submit the order and voluntary testimony. Request a formal ruling.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S11.D: “Do not call incomplete evidence a victory. Proceed with the identity inquiry.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S12.title: Do Not Call It Charity
Gu puts three clean agreements down. Pei crosses out the first heading: Charitable Assistance.
Pei: “These are wages and a settlement.”
You: “Then show us what's owed already and what's being offered on top.”
Pei: “The hundred and forty remains owed. Housing and work are additional.”
Pei: “The physician will assess what each person can manage before they're assigned copying or cloth sorting. Nobody will be handling ore.”
Pei: “We'll correct the deaths in a sealed register. I'll report my part in what happened and Gu will have to answer for the false entries he made.”
You: “The public never hears who ordered the exhaust shut.”
Pei: “Signing the final settlement means no further claim for this accident. That includes your hand if it never recovers.”
Tang: “Read that last answer to all six. Slowly.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S12.A: “Ask every claimant separately. Nobody waives someone else’s claim.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S12.B: “Let them consider leaving with their claims unresolved.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S12.C: “No settlement yet. Continue the identity inquiry with safe lodging.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S13.title: Two Rooms
Tang lays his sister’s reply beside the ferry booking: Two rooms. Six people. Bring bedding. No debt for the roof.
Tang: “She doesn’t promise meals forever. Neither do I.”
Pei: “I'll issue each of them a departure pass without asking them to give up the wages and compensation they're still owed.”
Pei: “I'll sign the release you asked for but I can't promise that another sect will take you in.”
Shao: “I'd rather you stayed and corrected the report. We can't do that for you across the river.”
Tang looks at Shao's splinted hand, then turns to check the cart's harness.
Tang: “I'll drive. We'll ask for help loading the tools; the heavy ones need to sit over the axle.”
Tang: “The free tool space is gone. People and bedding still fit. A separate cargo cart costs eight stones.”
Tang: “The tools are loaded. They won’t have to leave everything they can earn with.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S13.A: “Leave under the available terms, with their individual agreement.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S13.B: “I’ll pay eight stones to send the tools onward.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S13.C: “This is still precarious. Ask them to reconsider waiting for the inquiry.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S14.title: The Seventh Month
The six survivors and Duan, who has been asked to attend, check their separate agreements. Tang reads for anyone who needs him to. Nobody signs for someone still uncertain.
Duan: “My husband’s allowance is not payment for silence.”
Pei: “You don't have to sign away anything to be owed that allowance. This agreement lets me release it now while settling the additional accident claim you're being asked to give up.”
Duan: “Then write that distinction on mine.”
Shao: “Where are we supposed to live when those six months run out?”
Pei: “The lodging subsidy ends. Your paid work continues under its ordinary employment terms.”
Shao: “Don’t describe that as security for life.”
The seven claimants eventually agree, without cheering. Pei commits his accumulated stipend as security for the housing payments and cancels his next cultivation retreat.
Duan: “And when the six months are up, they'll still need somewhere to sleep.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S14.A: “I’ll witness these specific commitments, without calling them fair.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S14.B: “They have the right to sign. I won’t endorse the waiver; record my dissent under seal.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S15.title: Under His Own Name
At the ferry, Shao gives his departure pass to the boatkeeper himself.
He almost adds an explanation, then doesn’t.
Duan hands over the clean coat linings.
Duan: “You can use your own name now. They've put Jian's down correctly.”
Tang: “There’s space for your sewing box.”
Duan: “I’m staying. Someone has to open this shop tomorrow.”
Duan: “Write to me once you're settled so I can see your own name on a letter.”
The five other survivors board one at a time, helped according to their injuries. Nobody has recovered merely because the crossing is hopeful.
Tang looks back at the funeral cart he is leaving with a neighbor.
Tang: “He'll keep the cart for now. I'll come back for it once we're settled across the river.”
He holds the claim packet Pei certified. Identity and wage acknowledgments have been added; missing accident evidence has not magically appeared.
life.replacement.winter_coats.S15.A: “Leave the certified packet with Duan for her continuing claim.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S15.B: “Give the certified packet to Shao so they can pursue their claims later.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S16.title: Alive, but Not Free to Leave
Once the identity review begins, Tang writes an account in Duan's shop and lists the remaining uncertainties separately.
Tang: “Pei's arranged supervised lodging for all six while their identities are checked. They can speak to whoever they want but they can't leave yet and they won't be sent back into the gallery.”
Tang: “It's still being held because no settlement has been signed.”
Duan: “Then write that. Don’t call lodging wages.”
Tang: “I kept the evidence we actually had.”
Tang: “I'll record what was promised and what was done. If there was fighting, that gets a separate account too.”
She looks toward the place where she set the commission money.
Duan: “The report earned two stones. That doesn’t settle everything else.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S16.A: “Submit my named eyewitness account and make copies available to all six.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.S16.B: “I’ll report to Duan, but volunteer no further statement against the six.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.E1.title: No Longer an Unavoidable Accident
life.replacement.winter_coats.E1.en_us.0: The working gallery closes. Wages and the allowance are released; injury claims remain open. Gu faces a falsification inquiry, and Pei’s reassignment order joins the evidence against the managers.
life.replacement.winter_coats.E1.en_us.1: Duan: “They stopped calling Jian’s death an unavoidable accident.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.E1.en_us.3: Duan: “The clerk changed the wording on the record so I'm keeping the old copy beside the new one.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.E1.en_us.4: A neighbor stops buying cloth because his family depended on the closed mine. Duan understands his worry about winter, but cannot ask the injured to return to danger for him.
life.replacement.winter_coats.E1.en_us.5: Shao: “I'll testify. I just don't know how those families will get through the winter without the work.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.E1.en_us.7: You retain a copy of your testimony. No cultivation method comes with being believed. The case is real now. So are the people who wish you had left it buried.
life.replacement.winter_coats.E2.title: The First Payment Arrives
life.replacement.winter_coats.E2.en_us.0: The withheld hundred and forty stones are finally released, twenty to each of the seven claimants. Accommodation payments arrive on their separate schedule. None of this money is your fee.
life.replacement.winter_coats.E2.en_us.1: Shao: “I copied thirty inventory lines today.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.E2.en_us.3: Shao: “It started hurting and the physician told me to stop working. I'm still getting used to being allowed to do that.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.E2.en_us.4: Pei: “The exhaust controls have been replaced.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.E2.en_us.5: Duan: “And the man who ordered them shut?”
life.replacement.winter_coats.E2.en_us.6: Pei: “He's still employed but he no longer has any say in these workers' assignments.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.E2.en_us.7: She folds his explanatory letter along its original crease.
life.replacement.winter_coats.E2.en_us.8: Duan: “Next time you write, tell me whether he's still giving orders. I've had enough letters saying we've all made peace.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.E2.en_us.9: No celebration is arranged. The workers have names, wages, and beds. They have surrendered claims that might one day have bought much more—or never bought anything. Everyone signed with that uncertainty intact.
life.replacement.winter_coats.E3.title: No Miracle Across the River
life.replacement.winter_coats.E3.en_us.0: Tang sends news from across the river. Duan opens the letter beside her cutting table.
life.replacement.winter_coats.E3.en_us.1: Tang, letter: “The six are managing in the two rooms although there's hardly space to turn round. Ning has started repairing tally slips with his left hand while the others pick up whatever suitable work they can find. There isn't work every day so we save on fuel by cooking together.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.E3.en_us.2: A second hand appears below his.
life.replacement.winter_coats.E3.en_us.3: Shao, letter: “Duan, Jian swore when the door stuck. It's not something I'd usually put in a letter to you. But you asked us not to make him sound braver than he was, so I thought I should tell you.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.E3.en_us.6: The hundred and forty stones remain in disputed accounts upriver. The six have left coercive work, not injury or poverty. Gu stays to face his report. Whoever received the certified packet bears responsibility for preserving it for any future claim.
life.replacement.winter_coats.E4.title: Living People in an Inconvenient File
life.replacement.winter_coats.E4.en_us.0: The death register remains disputed. The six sleep under supervision while the inquiry moves through offices that have not seen their hands.
life.replacement.winter_coats.E4.en_us.1: Duan: “Do they know Jian really died?”
life.replacement.winter_coats.E4.en_us.2: Tang: “They've finally corrected the record to show that Jian really died.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.E4.en_us.3: Duan: “Good. I won’t have him alive when they need a signature and dead when they owe money.”
life.replacement.winter_coats.E4.en_us.4: This is not acquittal, compensation, or escape. It is six living people entered into an inconvenient file instead of disappearing into a convenient grave.
life.replacement.winter_coats.E4.en_us.5: A named witness’s statement remains in the case. A character who chose a private report has signed nothing additional for either side. An unconscious character is not assigned a conversation they never attended. If the simulated life ended, what remains is Tang’s account—not the dead speaking again.
life.replacement.ninth_spring.title: The Ninth Spring
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S01.title: Their Mother’s Awl
After giving you a night's lodging, Lu Shan invites you to breakfast and asks you to take an old family possession to his sister Mei. She worked in her master's workshop for eight years and has not come home since leaving last winter. Her master died six weeks ago, and Shan wants to hear what she intends to do. Lu Shan sets a red-handled awl beside your breakfast. The wood has been polished pale where a thumb would rest.
Shan: “It belonged to our mother before Mei borrowed it to take to Master Yu's.”
Shan: “I want you to take it to her. I found it in his returned belongings.”
You: “You gave me a bed to deliver an awl?”
Shan: “I'd like you to ask whether she's coming home and bring back whatever answer she gives you without trying to change her mind for me.”
Across Apricot Bridge, a chimney speaks in a cracked old voice. You cannot make out the words.
You: “I thought her master was dead.”
Shan: “We buried him six weeks ago and she was there. She's waiting for the lesson he'd promised her before he died.”
He wraps the awl, but leaves the parcel untied.
Shan: “Don't promise her a spirit root. That's how Master Yu kept her there. Don't give her another empty wait.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S01.B: “First, I’ll ask what the sect intends to take.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S02.title: Waiting for the Ninth Year
You find Mei beside the workshop and hand her the parcel. Opening it by a row of numbered wooden models, she recognizes her mother's red-handled awl.
Mei: “After my master took it away, I thought it was lost.”
You: “Your brother found it among the belongings sent back and asked me to return it.”
Mei: “Master said ordinary tools would teach me ordinary habits.”
Mei: “The hinges I made still work and so does the stove I repaired at home. I used to be proud of that before he made it sound like something I should be ashamed of.”
She sets the awl beside a broken model.
Mei: “I have no spirit root. You can stop looking for a polite way to ask.”
You: “Then what lesson are you waiting for?”
Mei: “He said the furnace could make one. Ninth spring.”
Mei: “It was supposed to be this spring but he sent me away over the winter and died before he could explain.”
The chimney repeats its cracked phrase. Her lips move through the missing word.
Mei: “Help me find what he finished. Not what you think he should have finished.”
You: “All right. Let me see the work first.”
Mei: “You’d be the first visitor this week.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S02.A: “Show me what matters. We’ll speak to Qin first.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S02.B: “I'll help examine the furnace after we find someone independent to assess it without experimenting on you.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S03.title: The Keeper in the Inventory
Shen Qiu, the sect steward responsible for recovering the core, is checking the workshop's contents at the entrance. His inventory lists the core, the trial book and eleven unreturned sect tools. Mei has a separate line: workshop keeper, unpaid.
Shen: “I tested her eight years ago.”
Shen: “The test showed she had no spirit root and I told him that at the time.”
He looks again at the word unpaid, then copies the whole line. He does not cross it out.
You: “Why not carry the furnace away?”
Shen: “Its inner reservoir still holds heat. Moving it under charge could break the street.”
Shen: “That helps me hold a cracked vessel. It doesn’t tell me which concealed pipe opens into someone’s kitchen.”
Shen: “Mei's the one who operates it every day and Qin laid the clay channels.”
Outside, someone waits with an unpaid tile invoice.
Shen: “The sect can pay to move the furnace. As for what Yu owed her for those eight years, we'll have to look at that too.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S03.A: “Supervise the inspection. Don’t decide for Mei.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S03.B: “First, establish where the clay channels go.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S04.title: Not a Spare Afternoon
You find Qin He, the workshop yard's owner, examining a removed clay sleeve. Having laid the furnace's channels herself, she notices that it is scorched outside rather than within.
Qin: “It’s feeding warmth back towards the operator’s seat.”
You: “Was it meant to do that?”
Qin: “I didn't design it. I laid the pipes, so I can show you where they lead.”
She points out scratches beneath the storage shutter and a discarded red scale. The tool chest stands beyond it on a scorched wooden platform.
Qin: “There's something nesting in the warm rubble that looks like an iron-scale scorpion. Keep your hands out of the gaps until we know where it is.”
Qin: “An afternoon. I’ll miss firing my tile order. Or six stones hires my waiting assistant and she fires it without me.”
Her thumb stays on the sleeve’s scorched surface.
Qin: “If you can't pay, I'll still help. But I'll lose the tile order, and I need you to understand that.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S04.A: “Please map it. I won’t pretend the missed order costs nothing.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S04.B: “I’ll pay six stones for the assistant to fire the tiles.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S04.C: “Leave the channels alone. Inspect the external controls and records.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S05.title: The Empty Chair
Before the inspection, you make sure the entrusted awl has reached Mei. She brings the trial book and sets a measuring cup beside the furnace. As the water heats, the brass ring beneath it darkens and the recording disc linked to the cooling valve begins replaying an old lesson.
Recording of Yu: “Place your hand above the cup. When the copper ring darkens, your seed is waking.”
Mei keeps her hands at her sides. The ring darkens anyway.
Qin: “Let's try it again with nobody holding their hands over the cup.”
Mei: “He said to stay perfectly still. For hours.”
You: “The last trial page says the ring changed with an empty chair.”
Mei: “Don’t read it over my shoulder. Give it here.”
Qin: “There’s a maintenance note. His final recorded word marks the shutter’s cool interval. We can use the voice as a timing guide.”
Mei: “Must we keep listening to him?”
You: “Not if you tell us to stop. It isn’t him answering.”
Mei: “I know. It's just… every time I hear it, I still wait for him to tell me what to do.”
Nobody touches the switch before she finishes reading.
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S05.A: “Only until we’ve dealt with the tool chest. Is that acceptable?”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S06.title: When He Knew
Once Shen joins the inspection, you examine the trial book together. Mei lays it on the cold bench and points out that the entry predates her dismissal by fourteen months.
Mei: “He knew.”
You: “At least by this date.”
Mei: “Read the next bit.”
You, reading Yu’s notes: “'I told her to wait another spring because I needed her to keep the workshop running. I let myself believe that needing her gave me the right to keep her here.'”
Mei: “Did he write that for me?”
You: “It doesn’t say.”
Mei: “Good. Don’t improve it.”
Shen: “This apparatus has not made a root. There is no working method hidden in this trial book.”
Mei: “Could a better cultivator—”
Shen: “I'm sorry but I don't know any method that would give you a root and nothing in this book changes that. You shouldn't have been made to wait for it.”
Mei: “I kept the reservoir steady for eight years.”
Qin: “Yes.”
Mei: “A mortal.”
Qin: “You did the work, Mei. We've all been relying on you to keep it running.”
Mei: “I can repair it.”
Shen: “You can repair its controls. That isn’t the same as making its promise true.”
Mei: “I know. I’m trying to work out which things are still mine.”
Shen: “The ordinary fittings and hand tools were left to you. The charged core remains sect property.”
Mei closes the book carefully and lays her mother's awl across the cover while the rest of you wait for her to speak.
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S06.A: “Bring your brother. Let him hear this from you.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S06.B: “Discuss what can actually be done, without deciding your whole future.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S06.C: “You can go home tonight and let Shen seal the furnace.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S07.title: The Grain Was Eaten
Shan arrives carrying Mei’s old bedding. It has been aired, not packed.
Mei: “You were sure I’d come.”
Shan: “I was sure it would smell terrible otherwise.”
Mei: “There’s no root.”
Shan: “I heard.”
Mei: “Don’t say you knew.”
Shan: “I didn’t. I hoped he knew something I didn’t.”
Mei: “You sent grain.”
Shan: “You were hungry.”
Mei: “I wasted it.”
Shan: “Did you eat it?”
Mei: “Yes.”
Shan: “Then that part worked.”
She lets out an angry laugh and buries her face in the aired blanket as Shan waits beside her without reaching for the book.
Mei: “I don’t know whether I want his workshop or want him to see me leave it.”
You: “He won't see it, Mei. But you can still decide what you want to do with it.”
Mei: “I could make something that wasn’t his.”
Shan: “You could also come home without making anything.”
Mei: “Give me until we make the furnace safe.”
Shan: “Then we'll talk again once you've made the furnace safe.”
He resumes folding the bedding but slows when he reaches the corner caught in her hand and leaves it loose.
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S07.A: “If you stay, let it be work you choose. I’ll help.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S07.B: “You don’t need to prove anything before going home.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S08.title: The Chest Is Still Inside
A deep tick interrupts the room. Shen clamps a new split in the reservoir, bracing it with his trained technique.
Shen: “Everyone away from the warm wall.”
Mei: “My models are in that chest.”
Shen: “The lane must stay clear. I can’t leave this clamp until we choose a shutdown.”
Shen: “The wall's getting hotter so we need to decide before we lose the chance to do anything.”
A red pincer appears beneath the shutter.
Mei: “Can you hold it while I go in?”
Qin: “The underside of the platform is burning through and it'll collapse under you if you climb onto it.”
Mei: “I know it won't give me a root. But those models are mine. I made them.”
Shen: “Only someone with a suitable practiced barrier can relieve me safely. Otherwise I stay here. Clear the rest of the lane.”
Qin checks that the bystanders have moved behind stone.
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S08.A: “I’ll examine the chest’s position before choosing a fight.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S08.B: “Let's check whether the barrier I've learned will let me hold the clamp safely.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S08.C: “Keep everyone out. We won’t trade a person for the chest.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S09.title: Two Different Handles
The scorpion probes the scorched platform with one pincer.
Qin: “Second shutter cages it away from the chest. But pull under load and it jams.”
Qin: “The screen will drop into place and lock the shelf so we can winch the chest out without going inside.”
Mei: “The disc’s last word marks it. Or your map shows the indicator.”
You: “Could you walk me through it?”
Mei: “I can guide you from behind the wall as long as you don't need me to climb back onto the platform.”
Mei flinches at the crack of its tail against the stone but stays where she is.
Mei: “I want those tools. I don’t want someone carried out instead.”
Qin: “The emergency shutter isolates the whole room immediately. It can’t support the platform.”
You: “So one handle saves the tools.”
Qin: “If we have a reliable timing reference. The other saves the lane and loses the box. Say which before touching either.”
The external winch’s rope is intact. Qin puts her hand on it.
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S09.A: “We'll lower the screen during the verified cool interval so we can winch the chest out safely.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S09.B: “I’ll drive it away from the platform.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S09.C: “We should seal the room even if that means leaving the chest inside.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S10.title: It Is Guarding a Nest
You enter through the cool doorway. The scorpion turns; its pincers scrape the stone.
Mei, behind the wall: “Don’t back towards the warm tiles.”
Qin: “It looks as though something's made a nest in the warm rubble Yu left behind.”
Mei: “Make it leave the platform. We can pull the chest from outside.”
Shen: “Come back behind the wall if you can't hold it off and we'll leave the chest where it is.”
Mei: “Already done. You don’t have to tell me twice.”
The scorpion lifts its tail. The retreat doorway remains clear.
Qin: “I’ve got the winch. Call when it’s clear. Don’t try to carry the chest while you’re fighting.”
Mei’s hand closes over the family awl. She stays out of the doorway.
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S10.B: “I'm withdrawing so we can seal the building before anyone else gets hurt.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S11.title: What Remains
With the storage doorway secured, Shen still holds the clamp. Mei stands where she can see all three external controls.
Shen: “Whole transfer, controlled dismantling, or destruction.”
Shen: “Transfer preserves the trial work. I can offer a paid mechanical assistant’s place. Not discipleship.”
Qin: “We could fit the ordinary shell with a wood-burning firebox to heat a repair shop. The spiritual core has to be deactivated here first. After that it would be an ordinary workshop.”
Qin: “The channel map, her saved measuring tools, and her agreement to do the work.”
Shen: “I'll supervise a quench that destroys the powered parts and the working research. We'll keep the page recording the failed trial so nobody mistakes what happened here.”
Mei: “What if I choose nothing today?”

Shen: “We'll seal and guard the building until the removal crew arrives. Recovered private belongings will be returned individually. Losses inside will be recorded too, separately from the sect's inventory.”
Mei requests that any remaining recording be erased. Qin does it.
Mei keeps watching the silent chimney as though she hasn't yet grown used to the absence of the recorded voice.
Mei: “I made those things myself. I keep forgetting that when I look at the furnace.”
Mei: “I know why we closed the door. I’m still allowed to grieve. Don’t make me choose between those.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S11.A: “Set out the transfer and employment terms.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S11.B: “Preserve the practical work, not the promise.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S11.C: “Discuss destruction rather than leaving the danger for another apprentice.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S11.D: “Let's seal it while she takes more time to decide.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S12.title: Not a Discipleship
Shen writes “mechanical assistant” where the inventory called Mei a keeper.
Mei: “A wage from the first day.”
Shen: “Yes.”
Mei: “Access to the trial record, including failures.”
Shen: “Within the supervised workshop.”
Mei: “No trials on me.”
Shen: “There won't be any human trials with this prototype. I'll put that in writing.”
Mei: “And after a year?”
Shen: “You're free to leave after the year with your personal models. Anything developed as part of your paid work will belong to the sect.”
You: “Will she be taught?”
Shen: “Scheduled lessons in measurement and instrument repair. There is no cultivation method in that offer.”
Mei: “Then stop calling me fortunate.”
Shen: “I haven’t.”
Mei: “You looked ready to.”
Shen crosses out an unfinished sentence.
You: “Who carries the reservoir?”
Shen: “Once it's stable I'll bring in trained handlers to move it rather than ask her to carry it.”
Mei: “And I can decline the job without surrendering my tools?”
Shen: “Yes. You can agree to transfer the equipment without taking the job. I'll arrange the handlers separately.”
Mei reads that clause twice.
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S12.A: “These specific terms are worth witnessing, not a promise to change your root.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S12.B: “You can hand over the furnace without handing over your next year.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S12.C: “Before we sign I'd like to discuss destroying it instead.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S13.title: A Workshop That Is Not His
Qin chalks a line around the ordinary furnace jacket. Mei’s recovered gauges lie beside the map.
Qin: “This stays. The charged center doesn’t.”
Mei: “People will call it his workshop.”
Qin: “Only if you leave his name over the door.”
Shen: “Follow the map. No guessed techniques in place of instructions.”
Mei: “Eight years. I thought I’d come back flying.”
Mei: “A hinge that doesn’t catch my sleeve.”
Mei: “Can I work here without you owning me?”
Qin: “You can rent a bench here for as long as it suits you and leave when you want to.”
Mei: “I can afford the bench after I finish three paid repairs. Not before.”
Qin: “You can start paying rent once you've finished those three repairs and we'll put that in writing before you begin.”
Mei reaches for paper to record the terms while Shen holds the clamp steady until the agreed shutdown begins.
Mei: “I’ll help ten afternoons with the next batch. It won’t repay the sale. I just won’t let this become more work you did for nothing.”
Qin: “Separate from the bench rent. That’s the agreement—not owing me forever.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S13.A: “I’ll return for two afternoons of ordinary work.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S13.B: “I’ll pay six stones for hired help with the refitting.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S13.C: “I’ll witness your agreement without promising work I cannot provide.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S14.title: Permission to Let It Go
Mei separates the failure report from the other trial pages.
Mei: “Burning these won’t make him kinder.”
Mei: “Keeping them won’t give the eight years back.”
Shan unfolds the blanket over her shoulders.
Shan: “You don't have to explain it to us. If you want to stop, say so.”
Shen: “The destructive quench leaves even the ordinary jacket unusable. We can still stop.”
Mei: “Keep the report. No one gets to rediscover his failure and sell it as my chance.”
Still holding the external clamp, Shen asks Qin to confirm that the lane is clear before preparing the shutdown.
Shen: “Once you tell me to proceed everyone stays outside until it's done. Nobody goes back to try the cup one last time.”
Mei: “You won't have to worry about me going back to that cup.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S14.A: “Keep the failure report publicly accessible, then end the experiment.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S14.B: “Preserve the safety record without publishing her private history.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S14.C: “I'd rather seal it than make the final decision today.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S15.title: Only Tonight
Qin records the exchange for anyone unable to take part.
Qin: “Everyone's out and the house is sealed with Shen keeping watch until the removal crew arrives.”
Qin: “At my table. With her awl and whatever work we got out.”
Shan: “Did she say she was coming home?”
Mei: “That isn’t a decision about the rest of my life.”
Shan: “I heard the first two words.”
Shen: “Under my seal. Your right to inspect it is recorded.”
Qin: “I'll check which tools we got out. And if anyone's hurt, we still need to get them seen to.”
Shan: “We've got enough to worry about tonight.”
Qin: “I know. I'll go and check.”
There is room beneath the account for a conscious witness’s own decision.
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S15.A: “Submit my named account for review of the false promises and failed oversight.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.S15.B: “Leave the family a truthful report without signing another commitment.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E1.title: Failure, Written Down
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E1.en_us.0: The contained furnace leaves under escort. Mei has read the second inventory copy.
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E1.en_us.1: Shen meets her at a workbench, not a testing stool.
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E1.en_us.3: Mei: “I'm checking that the valve moves with the handle instead of lagging behind it.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E1.en_us.4: Shen: “What if it starts moving before you touch the handle?”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E1.en_us.5: Mei: “I'll stop and find out what's wrong before I try it again.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E1.en_us.6: Shen: “Write the fault before repairing it.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E1.en_us.7: Mei: “Even if the whole project turns out useless?”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E1.en_us.9: Mei remains a mortal, with a wage and a year’s contractual obligation—not a promised root.
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E1.en_us.1: Mei: “It can go on without me.”
Shan: “It did a poor job of that before.”
Mei: “That isn’t a reason to follow it.”
Mei: “Tell them to ask me when I get back. I haven't worked out what to say yet either.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E2.title: A Door That Does Not Need Kicking
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E2.en_us.0: The replacement wood-burning firebox warms the repair bench. Mei marks the holes with her red-handled awl before fitting the new hinge to the door.
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E2.en_us.2: Mei: “No. It opens when you push it.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E2.en_us.3: Customer: “Then what am I paying for?”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E2.en_us.5: The customer tests it twice, then pays Qin.
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E2.en_us.6: Qin: “We'll keep a record in this column of each job you finish.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E2.en_us.7: Mei: “Let's agree how future jobs are paid before we do them. I don't want finished work turning into another favor.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E2.en_us.8: Mei: “I'll give you the ten afternoons we agreed on even though I know it won't make up for the order you lost.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E2.en_us.9: Qin: “No. But you can help me fill the next one.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E2.en_us.1: Qin: “We kept the order. You don’t owe me invented afternoons.”
Qin: “Tell people what you can actually teach.”
Above the bench Mei hangs a sign: Repairs. Under it: Lessons by agreement.
Mei: “Hinges, for a start. I could teach someone to make one of these.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E3.title: No Longer Waiting for It to Bloom
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E3.en_us.0: The quench destroys the sealed core and working research. Even the ordinary jacket is unusable. The retained report begins with failure, not Yu’s titles.
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E3.en_us.1: Mei: “I don’t know what I’m supposed to feel.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E3.en_us.5: Shen: “The safety account will say this apparatus failed. Not that no future researcher could ever succeed.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E3.en_us.6: Mei: “That's all right as long as they understand I won't be waiting beside this furnace anymore.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E3.en_us.7: Qin: “Take the private belongings we've checked. My hammer stays here—don't pack it with the rest.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E3.en_us.8: Mei: “I know which handle you repaired.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E3.en_us.1: Mei walks with her brother because the road is open and she has chosen it.
Mei: “Tell them what I agreed to tell them. If they want to know how I'm taking it, they can wait.”
The awl remains in her pocket. There is no inheritance of stored cultivation.
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E4.title: Going Home Is Not a Verdict
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E4.en_us.0: Qin’s next written account contains no miracle. The furnace remains under a maintained sect seal; Mei sleeps at her brother’s house.
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E4.en_us.1: Shan: “She asked where ordinary tools are sold.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E4.en_us.3: Shan: “I asked whether she wanted company.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E4.en_us.5: Mei: “I haven’t decided about the workbench.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E4.en_us.8: Shan: “I know. I just wanted you to know there's still a bed.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E4.en_us.9: Shen: “The trial book is still available for your inspection.”
life.replacement.ninth_spring.E4.en_us.1: Mei: “I'll come back when I feel ready instead of waiting outside every morning.”
No job has been accepted and no dangerous lesson restarted.
Qin writes: “A named complaint was submitted only if our witness authorized it. Otherwise the report stays with the family. No one signs for an unconscious person.”
For a deceased protagonist, this is a legacy account. For a living one, the story ends without deciding the rest of either person’s life.
life.replacement.salt_baskets.title: The Empty Salt Baskets
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S01.title: Seventeen Households
Ruan Qiao is collecting a joint order for seventeen households, but their three salt baskets have not come down the mountain. The driver Tian Rang and the sect deer in his care are missing too. She invites you into the shop to explain the job and its accounts. Ruan Qiao puts three wooden salt tallies on the counter. Rain has not reached the village yet; above it, the old pack road is already shedding stones.
Ruan: “Each basket holds a sealed sack of salt worth six stones. Seventeen households paid for the three together.”
Ruan: “Tian Rang. Find him before someone decides an empty saddle means bandits.”
You: “You sound as though you expect another answer.”
Ruan: “I want to hear it from him. People are already saying all sorts of things.”
She sets down a separate purse.
Ruan: “Here's six stones for the freight. Keep track of what you spend and bring the rest back.”
Ruan: “I'll pay you three stones for telling me what happened however unwelcome the news turns out to be.”
A child outside is shaking a toy bell. Ruan goes to the doorway and asks him to put it away for now.
Ruan: “Rang calls his deer with that sound. If it's frightened, we don't want to draw it into a crowd.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S02.title: The Knife Cut
At the broken stretch of path you find Rang's apprentice Ye Sui beside a cut strap. Salt remains between the stones. As you approach, she puts her hand over the traces.
Ye: “Because I said there were bandits.”
Ye: “I never saw bandits. My master told me to say that, so I did. I didn't even look for tracks.”
Two sealed sacks are caught behind a fallen pillar on the ledge she points to below. The third has split open and spilled its salt into the stream.
Ye: “The old steps reach them. Four stones hires the porters waiting at the shrine. Or someone able can take the whole afternoon.”
Ye: “Its name is Eleven. The hoofprints go uphill without drag marks beside them. It seems to have walked there itself.”
You: “Why would Rang leave the salt?”
Ye: “Ask him before you call him a thief.”
She stands beside the uphill path without reaching to stop you.
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S03.title: A Bond, Not a Bounty
Xu Ce is arranging the last grain convoy before the storm. He checks two handlers’ straps himself. Ye waits beside the scales.
Xu: “I approved a load of three sacks on the understanding that the saddle was fit to carry them.”
Xu: “I know now. Ye showed me the broken buckle.”
Xu: “A frightened Qi Refining beast is loose above occupied houses.”
Xu: “Perhaps. Chasing it onto a roof would still be my mistake.”
He returns one load to the scales.
Xu: “Rang lodged eighteen stones as his route bond. It pays verified cargo losses first. It is not a price on his animal.”
Xu: “The sect owns him, but Rang raised him. Rang doesn't like being reminded of the first part.”
He puts a blank order beside the inkstone.
Xu: “I can suspend capture until tomorrow’s hearing. I cannot suspend the villagers’ losses.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S03.B: “We should record what's missing before bringing up the salt we can save.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S04.title: Who Understood the Promise?
At the ruined watchhouse, Ye washes dried blood off the saddle’s lining. Beneath it, the broken buckle has folded inward like a hook.
Ye: “He said Eleven only needed a new pad.”
Ye: “I wanted him to know more than me.”
Ye: “I know. I should have said something when I saw it.”
She lays the strap where you can see it without touching the stained fabric.
Ye: “Rang promised last autumn would be Eleven’s last carrying season. Then he accepted the winter route.”
You: “Did the deer understand the promise?”
A hoof scrapes inside. She lowers her voice, not because the animal understands the words, but because it watches every raised hand.
Ye: “He'll talk to us at dusk once the patrol's passed. I'd like him to have that chance before anyone leads Eleven away and I'll admit what I said about the bandits.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S04.A: “No forced removal before the hearing. I’ll wait.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S04.B: “Correct it in your own words. Then we salvage.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S05.title: What Can Be Carried Back
The shortcut beneath the ruined shrine is collapsing, but the longer stone steps remain intact. Two porters waiting nearby bring their own carrying frames to inspect the job. One checks the straps while the other examines the return route.
Porter: “We can bring these two up. The third's gone; there's nothing we can do about that.”
Porter: “You can bring Ruan wet sand. I wouldn’t.”
Ye: “Would you take the long steps rather than risk the narrow way down?”
You: “What happens if we leave them?”
Porter: “Tonight’s runoff takes the shelf. Decide while there is still a shelf.”
You: “The seals on both sacks match Ruan's tallies and neither's been opened.”
Ye: “I helped hide the truth. Those sacks belong to the households. Getting them back doesn't make up for what I said.”
Ye waits beside the stone railing while you decide who will carry the salt.
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S05.A: “Hire the porters with the freight purse.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S05.C: “Use a movement technique I already know.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S05.D: “Let's find Rang before we try to recover the salt.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S06.title: “One More Trip”
By the time you reach the watchhouse dusk has settled around Eleven's bare and rubbed flank. He bears weight evenly on all four legs while Rang grips the familiar route bell through the cloth wrapped around it.
Rang: “Don’t ring it.”
You: “Ruan said the same.”
Rang: “He’ll come even when he shouldn’t.”
You: “You cut the loads loose.”
Rang: “The hook caught his flank and he reared so close to the edge that I cut the loads free before they pulled him over.”
You: “And then hid.”
Rang: “I couldn’t lead him back to the saddle.”
Ye: “You could have sent me with the truth.”
Rang: “Yes.”
You: “Why did you load him after seeing blood?”
Rang: “I thought I could finish once.”
Ye: “You said that last winter.”
Rang: “My roof leaks, and I still owe Ruan a replacement for the shed beam Eleven cracked. I needed money, so I took another run.”
You: “He needed somewhere to rest too.”
Rang: “I know what I’ve done.”
Ye: “Knowing hasn’t stopped you yet.”
Eleven presses his muzzle against Rang’s sleeve. Rang withdraws the wrapped bell before the animal can reach it.
Rang: “I've looked after him since he was a calf and I don't want you to think all those years meant nothing.”
You: “You raised him. Why did you put the saddle on when you knew he was hurt?”
Rang: “I shouldn't have. I kept thinking he'd manage because he always had before.”
When rain begins tapping the roof, he wraps the bell tightly and puts it in his bag instead of holding it.
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S06.B: “Let's ask Ruan to join us so we can discuss the lost salt and Eleven's care.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S06.C: “I'll take your answer back without deciding what you should do.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S07.title: Seeing Deer Is Not Finding a Route
At dawn, Ye takes you above the watchhouse. Beyond the ridge, three wild cliff deer move between pines. The old north path avoids the village fields, but its last bend is hidden.
Ye: “He lived among other deer before the sect bought that herd.”
You: “That doesn’t mean they’ll welcome him.”
Ye: “It gives us somewhere to start looking even if we don't yet know whether he'll be accepted.”
You: “What happens if we stop here?”
Ye: “We'd have to report that we saw deer but couldn't establish a safe route for him.”
When a loose tile falls from the watchhouse Eleven moves away without bolting and Rang lets the lead stay slack rather than pulling him back by the neck.
Ye: “See? He can choose a quieter place.”
Ye: “Yes. I’m not asking you to call that the same thing as a mountain.”
She waits for your decision before taking the narrow path.
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S08.title: Not Payment
Ruan arrives with the morning porters. Rainwater has scoured the salt ledge overnight. She checks what actually came back before facing Rang.
Ruan: “Three sacks. Which households did you decide could lose theirs?”
Rang: “I didn’t choose households.”
Ruan: “You chose not to tell them.”
Rang: “Yes.”
You: “His bond can cover the missing salt.”
Ruan: “At six a sack. Not a penalty I invent because I’m angry.”
Ye: “And Eleven?”
Ruan: “Not payment.”
Rang: “You'd let it stay in the village?”
Ruan: “He could stay in my fenced lower orchard for twelve stones including winter fodder. We'd need to agree again before he stayed beyond the winter.”
Rang: “If two sacks came back, that’s what remains of my bond.”
Ruan: “If we haven't recovered the two sacks the whole bond goes towards the missing salt.”
Ye: “The sect has a retirement paddock.”
Rang: “Far away.”
Ruan: “Far away isn’t the same as dead.”
You: “There’s also the north ridge.”
Ruan: “A release needs a checked route. Not an animal pushed behind my cabbages.”
She pays your three-stone commission, then keeps the freight purse separate on her knee.
Ruan: “You'll get your fee for the report. But let the households decide what they're willing to accept.”
Ruan: “I'm glad the salt's back. We still missed yesterday's market, though. I'll have to explain that to the households.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S08.B: “We'll show them the suspension order and ask Xu to come here.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S09.title: The Lead Rope
Two search escorts meet you at the lower gate. Their lead rope has no saddle attached, but Eleven stops when he sees it.
Escort: “We take the registered beast to supervised holding.”
Escort: “The order doesn’t require waiting for that.”
You: “We're asking Xu to hear the case.”
Escort: “I'll need to see the suspension order before I can let him stay here instead of taking him into supervised holding.”
Ye moves behind the stone wall with Eleven. Rang follows her rather than standing in front of the animal’s horns.
Ruan: “Nobody ties a rope to that sore flank.”
Rang: “That's what I was told last time, before the saddle went back on.”
The escorts leave enough room to pass without approaching Eleven. Neither draws a weapon yet.
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S09.B: “I'll accompany him if you record where he's being held.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S10.title: He Does Not Fight for You
You lead the confrontation into the empty cart yard away from Eleven and the bystanders as the two escorts follow with their weapons drawn.
Escort: “Let us through so we can take him into holding until the hearing.”
You: “Then let the hearing happen first.”
Ruan: “Eleven needs to stay behind the wall where he won't get caught in the fighting.”
Rang keeps the bell wrapped. For once, he does not call Eleven towards trouble.
Ye: “The gate behind you is open.”
Ruan: “And stop when the fighting stops. Winning this won’t buy back the salt.”
The younger escort glances at the rope he has put down, then at his partner. Nobody advances until you decide whether to stand down or commit.
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S10.B: “I'll stand down if his supervised holding is properly recorded.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S11.title: Two Separate Decisions
Xu examines Eleven in the enclosed yard. The injury is beneath the saddle; the animal walks without a limp. Xu makes no claim to have healed it.
Xu: “No more carrying. I will put that in every retirement order.”
You: “They haven’t felt separate to him.”
Xu: “Then we make them separate now.”
Xu: “We'll deduct six stones for each sack lost and return whatever's left of the bond to Rang.”
Ye: “Does being wrong cost him the right to speak?”
Ruan: “No. It costs him the money we lost.”
Xu: “The village can winter him with agreed funding. The station has an approved paddock place. Or I can authorize release if the route and his fitness for unladen travel are verified.”
Xu: “The sect has to agree, and so does whoever takes him in. We need to hear from both.”
You: “And if we agree on none?”
Xu: “Supervised holding while a retirement review continues. No saddle during that review.”
Xu writes the condition into the order while Ye notices Eleven reaching towards the trough and brings it closer so he doesn't have to move.
Rang: “You said no removal before the hearing. Bringing him back now doesn’t mean that promise was never broken.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S12.title: One Winter
Ruan takes you to the orchard below the village. Rang checks the fence beside the fodder shed and measures the latch that needs replacing. Eleven waits outside the gate.
Ruan: “Twelve stones. Winter ends at the spring fair.”
Ruan: “We make another agreement. Don’t promise him my land for life.”
Rang: “I can mend carts while he’s here.”
Ye: “You can earn by mending carts. That isn’t proof the money will last.”
Ruan: “I can watch from my house above the gate and Xu will hold a signed copy of the agreement so anyone who sees another saddle can report it.”
Ruan: “Don't put one on him at all, Rang. You know what I'm asking.”
He puts the broken buckle on her table, then returns to measuring the latch.
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S12.C: “We can't afford the care here so we should discuss taking him to the station.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S13.title: She Is Not Part of the Harness
Xu reads the station’s retirement terms aloud. Eleven’s place is funded from the existing herd budget, not from Ye’s wages.
Xu: “He won't be carrying packs or riders and nobody will force him to jump for a demonstration.”
Xu: “There is one six-month caretaker vacancy. Paid. Accepting it is separate from Eleven’s place.”
Ye: “I’m not part of his harness.”
Ye: “You did teach me. I'm still allowed to take a job somewhere else.”
The yard becomes quiet enough to hear Eleven chewing.
You: “What happens when her term ends?”
Xu: “The station will keep caring for him whether she stays in the job or leaves.”
Ye: “I won’t sign ‘for as long as the animal needs me.’ He may need someone for years.”
Ye: “I'll write when I can. But don't ask me to report everything he does.”
Xu leaves the employment page beside, not beneath, the retirement order.
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S13.A: “I’ll give an honest reference for your work.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S13.B: “Let the station supply its own keeper.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S13.C: “Do not sign a final arrangement yet.”
life.replacement.salt_baskets.S14.title: What Release Promises
The checked north route ends beyond the cultivated slopes. Xu watches Eleven walk it unladen before deciding that this journey is within his present ability.
Xu: “The wound still needs watching. Being able to walk unladen doesn't remove the risks of the mountain.”
Ruan: “I'll open the upper gate to let him through and close it again once he's clear.”
Ye: “Then we'll have to deal with it. He won't understand where the boundary is because we signed a paper.”
You: “What does the release actually promise?”
Xu: “We relinquish ownership. We don’t secretly keep him available for another route.”
Rang takes the wrapped bell from his bag, hesitates with a hand on the cloth, then unwraps it and passes it to Ye.
Rang: “Keep it out of my pocket.”
She takes it without calling that forgiveness.
